# 008 · INT8 post-training quantization of MobileCLIP2-B and S0 on the S22 (rerun of 007)

## Conclusions
**Bottom line: default post-training quantization (AI Hub quantize job, min-max calibration on 256 images /
512 captions from RefCOCOg train) is not usable for these models on the S22. It fails on accuracy, on compilation,
and on the device.** This is a negative result, recorded in full. The fp32 rows above are the reference: the "fp32"
QNN models already run in FP16 on the S22 NPU.

**On the device** (all job statuses and messages: `aihub_job_statuses.json`; the run reused the 8 successful quantize
jobs from 007):
- All 8 quantize jobs succeeded.
- **S0 image (w8a8 and w8a16): compile fails.** "QNN ONNX EP converter: cannot capture the entire model, got 31
  QNN-compatible subgraphs", so some quantized MCi/FastViT ops are not supported on the HTP.
- **All 4 text encoders and B image w8a16: compile succeeds, then every profile/inference job fails** with
  `QnnModel_composeGraphsFromDlc: MODEL_GRAPH_ERROR`. The graph can't be instantiated on the S22's HTP (v69).
  (S0 text w8a16 profile runs 1–2 were still queued when the script finished; run 0 failed with this error.)
- **Only B image w8a8 runs:** 13.71 ms vs 14.43 ms fp32, **just 5% faster**, with device output cosine to fp32
  of only 0.19 (mean 0.31). Its accuracy is destroyed.
- The `nan` totals in the combinations table mean "no S22 latency available" for that encoder.

**Accuracy** (onnxruntime on the downloaded QDQ ONNX, all 1,500 RefCOCOg-LPCVC queries; fp32 B = 71.31, S0 = 69.17):

| Encoder | w8a8 | w8a16 |
|---|---|---|
| B image (text fp32) | 5.03 (collapsed) | **71.31 (−0.01)** |
| B text (image fp32) | 1.50 (collapsed) | 4.76 (collapsed) |
| S0 image (text fp32) | 16.37 (collapsed) | **68.50 (−0.67)** |
| S0 text (image fp32) | 1.57 (collapsed) | **68.85 (−0.32)** |
| S0 both | 1.54 | **68.15 (−1.02, significant)** |

- **8-bit activations break every encoder.** That fits the known activation outliers in CLIP-style transformers
  (LayerNorm inputs, attention logits), which per-tensor min-max INT8 can't represent.
- **16-bit activations are nearly lossless**, except for B's text encoder. A plausible cause, not verified: B's text
  tower uses a causal attention mask, an additive constant with very large negative values. Quantizing it to int16
  with a min-max range destroys the masking. S0's text tower has no causal mask (`no_causal_mask=True`) and survives.
- The ORT simulation doesn't match the phone closely either (B image w8a8: cosine device vs ORT-QDQ 0.30).

**Decisions:**
1. Stop pursuing default PTQ for latency. The only quantized graph that runs saves 5%, because the float path
   already uses FP16 on the NPU. Quantization stays in the report as a measured negative result with the failure
   analysis above.
2. The leaderboard ranks by accuracy, and we have 17 ms of headroom with B. **Spend the remaining time on accuracy:
   fine-tuning or distillation of B (and S0 as the efficient model) on LPCVC-style data.**
3. Optional, if time allows: mixed-precision PTQ that keeps LayerNorm/softmax/attention-mask in FP16 (AIMET, or the
   quantize job's per-layer options) on S0's text tower and B's image tower. That's the only path with a chance of
   a real speedup at no accuracy cost.
4. Code fix (this commit): the scripts now wait for profile jobs and report device-side failure messages instead
   of a `KeyError`.
